note: Months are this site's suggestion wherever the plan names none: jobs done twice a year sit in March and November, when the clocks change; jobs done every three months sit in January, April, July and October; once-a-year jobs sit in January with the annual review. Move any of them to dates you will remember. A job the plan ties to a season or a month keeps it.
monthly_intro: A few minutes, on a day you pick.
dated_intro: These follow a date printed on the thing, the date on a paper, or something that happens. Put each date in your own calendar when you do the action.

entries.text: Press the test button on every smoke alarm.
Press the test button on every carbon monoxide alarm.
Look in and around the food bins for droppings or chewed corners.
Time yourself getting the pet into its carrier or onto its leash and to the exit.
Charge every power bank back to full.
Check the dates on stored food and move anything within six months of its date into the kitchen.
Refresh the backup copy on the external drive.
Talk the plan through with everyone at home.
Repeat the rehearsal as a game with young children.
Check the sizes of the diapers and clothes in the infant and toddler add-on.
Check the baby’s or small child’s sizes in the home kit.
Swap the contents of the overnight bag left at childcare.
Test the power kit: switch on every light and radio, charge the power banks and power stations, check the batteries, recharge the rechargeable cells and press each power-failure light’s test button.
entries.every: twice a year, when the clocks change

entries.text: Empty each grab bag: swap the clothing for the season, check sizes, replace anything that expires within six months and update the document copies.
entries.every: twice a year, when the clocks change

entries.text: Check the expiration date on every package in the medicine cabinet and replace anything out of date or nearly so.
Replace stored tap water: empty, clean, refill and write the new date.
Run a home fire drill.
Repeat the leave-the-home drill from other rooms and by your second way out.
Test the battery, hand-crank or solar radio.
Try every window and note which ones open and how far.
Replace the water, snacks and medicine in the kit at work, and swap the warm layer or sun hat for the season.
Take a new photo of each child, and one of you together.
Swap the pet food in the pet bag for fresh.
Check the pet’s ID tag can still be read.
Check the fit of the spare leash, collar and harness.
Check dates and batteries in an older relative’s supplies.
entries.every: each visit, or at least twice a year

entries.text: Replace the 9-volt backup battery in any smoke alarm that has one.
Work through the annual review sheet.
entries.every: once a year, on a date you will remember

entries.text: Walk one stairwell down and back up with your bags and headlamps.
Replace anything used or past its date in the home first-aid kit.
Check your second way to pay has not expired and that you know its PIN.
Update the Household sheet.
Swap the utility bill in your papers for a newer one.
Check every adult’s emergency alert registration.
entries.every: once a year, and when you move

entries.text: Retake the pet photos.
Replace the one bottle of plain bleach you keep for treating water, cans that got wet and the dish line.
Check the water-heater straps are still tight.
Flush the water heater, following the maker’s instructions.
Hold one stair walk or building drill.
Read a credit report from each bureau.
Collect the new IRS Identity Protection PIN.
Each adult pays each essential bill alone, with no shared password.
Buy flood insurance well before storm season: many policies take effect only 30 days after you buy them.
Ask the doctor about smoke days and check reliever inhalers and medicines are stocked.
Check the expiration dates on sunscreen and insect repellent and replace them.
Check each school and childcare pick-up list.
Have the wood stove or fireplace and its chimney cleaned and inspected.
entries.every: every year, before you count on it

entries.text: Fit the window-film kit over the warm room’s windows.
Find the water shut-off valves and ask how the building’s pipes are protected.
Add the winter items to the car kit and keep the tank near full.
Check the sizes of everyone’s warm clothes.
Do the ShakeOut drill on the third Thursday of October, check the bags and replace anything out of date.
Replace any smoke alarm more than 10 years past the date of manufacture printed on its back.
Replace the carbon monoxide alarm by the date its maker gives.
Replace the fire extinguisher at the date on its label, or after any use.
Replace the spare batteries by the date printed on the pack.
Replace sealed bottled water before its printed date, and drink the old bottles.
Replace the pet’s sealed water bottles by the date printed on them.
Renew the short-term care authority for your children before the paper runs out.
Illinois: sign a new short-term guardian appointment before the old one ends.
Michigan: sign a new delegation of parental powers before the old one runs out.
Illinois: renew the declaration for mental health treatment.
Michigan: reaffirm the MI-POST form.
entries.every: every year, and after any change the state lists

entries.text: Book the first-aid and CPR course again before the certificate lapses.
Review each child’s part of the plan.
Update each child’s dose on the medication list as the child grows: ask the doctor or pharmacist.
Refill prescriptions on the first day allowed and use the oldest first.
Update the one-page medical summary.
Print a fresh set of recovery codes.
entries.every: whenever you use one or change phones

entries.text: Review and update or re-sign every legal paper affected.
entries.every: after a move, marriage, divorce, birth or death

entries.text: Recheck beneficiaries and account owners.
entries.every: after a marriage, divorce, birth or death

entries.text: Re-check the library links, and reprint any document that has a newer edition.
